title: mappingAS • IUCN Criterion B screening
text: EOO = area minimum convex polygon points (≥ 3 unique coordinates; otherwise NA), edges densified along great circles measured WGS84 ellipsoid. AOO = number occupied 2 × 2 km cells × 4 km² (cell size via cell_km), taken minimum several translated grids. Subpopulations = circular-buffer method: circle radius subpop_resol_km (default 1/10 maximum inter-point distance, Rivers et al. 2010) drawn around occurrence, circles dissolved, disjoint polygons counted. Locations = number occupied cells 10 km grid (loc_km, sliding-scale fraction max inter-point distance via loc_scale), minimum translated grids. protected = TRUE, occurrences inside protected areas decoupled outside (ConR method_protected: "no_more_than_one" counts protected area occurrences one location; "" grids inside/outside separately). grid-based screening proxy, formal count locations specific threat. subpopulation location methods follow spatial rationale popularised ConR package (Dauby et al. 2017), cited idea; mappingAS implementation independent code. Areas measured data-centred Lambert Azimuthal Equal-Area projection, line IUCN guidelines. Conversion: land-cover classes grouped natural, anthropic, water, observed . headline index converted_pct = anthropic / (anthropic + natural) × 100 (terrestrial denominator; water -observed excluded default — set water_in_denominator = TRUE include water). Criterion B thresholds (screening ): EOO < 100 / 5,000 / 20,000 km² AOO < 10 / 500 / 2,000 km² CR / EN / VU. Applied Criterion B category (category_B / iucn_criterion_B()): combines size thresholds sub-criteria, following ConR’s selection logic. number locations caps category sub-criterion () — CR needs single location, EN ≤ 5, VU ≤ 10 — small range spread many locations held less threatened level location count supports (NT exceeds every threshold). continuing decline (b) , documented, inferred measured habitat loss — range holds converted (anthropic) cover, b(iii) taken met (decline_basis = "inferred (habitat loss)"). explicit IUCN backing: Guidelines (v16, §4.6) allow continuing decline habitat inferred “rate habitat loss” B1b/B2b, rate — magnitude threshold continuing decline Criterion B (Criterion C1 one). conversion available falls back global assumption ("assumed", ConR-style). Pass infer_decline_from_habitat = FALSE, assume_decline = FALSE decline = FALSE stricter “NT documented” screening.

code: occ <- read_occurrences(system.file("extdata", "example_occurrences.csv",                                     package = "mappingAS")) res <- assess_species(occ, mapbiomas = FALSE, verbose = FALSE) cat(assessment_report(res, output = "text")) #> Preliminary Conservation Assessment #> IUCN Red List Criterion B screening (provisional) - generated on 2026-10-11 with the mappingAS R package. #> Species: Prepusa connata Gardner #>  #> OVERVIEW AND EXECUTIVE STATUS #> This document reports a preliminary, size-based screening of Prepusa connata Gardner against Criterion B of the IUCN Red List Categories and Criteria. It is intended for screening only and does not constitute a formal Red List assessment. #> It is based on 5 occurrence records (5 with unique coordinates). The combined provisional category, from range size alone, is EN (B1 size). #> The category is driven not by range size alone but by its combination with a spatially concentrated pattern of occupation and active threat vectors (below). The most defensible full-criterion formulation would pair this size-based category with subconditions (a) few locations and (b) continuing decline in habitat quality, contingent on the validation set out in the recommendations. #>  #> GEOGRAPHIC RANGE METRICS #> The Extent of Occurrence (EOO), estimated as the area of the minimum convex polygon enclosing all occurrence points, is 2,461.73 km2. The Area of Occupancy (AOO), the number of occupied 2x2 km cells scaled to the IUCN 2x2 km reference, is 16.00 km2 (4 occupied cells). #> Both areas were measured on a data-centred Lambert Azimuthal Equal-Area projection, in line with the IUCN guidelines. #> As additional Criterion B evidence, the number of subpopulations is estimated at 4 (circular-buffer method) and the number of locations at 4 (occupied 10x10 km grid cells). These estimates use the same spatial rationale as the ConR package and are preliminary screening aids, not a formal count of locations under a specific threat. #>  #> PROVISIONAL CRITERION B CATEGORY #> Under the size thresholds of Criterion B, the EOO corresponds to EN (B1 size) (sub-criterion B1) and the AOO to EN (B2 size) (sub-criterion B2). The combined provisional category is EN (B1 size). #> Thresholds are CR / EN / VU for EOO < 100 / 5,000 / 20,000 km2 (B1) and AOO < 10 / 500 / 2,000 km2 (B2). These reflect range size only and, by themselves, do not qualify a taxon for listing: a formal Criterion B assessment additionally requires at least two of the subconditions (severe fragmentation or few locations, continuing decline, and extreme fluctuation). #> Both subcriteria converge on the same category, which strengthens the provisional attribution and makes it robust to moderate changes in either metric. #>  #> APPLIED CRITERION B CATEGORY #> Combining the size thresholds with the sub-criteria set for this assessment, the applied Criterion B category is EN (EN B1+2ab). The sub-criteria considered met are: (a) severe fragmentation / few locations, (b) continuing decline (assumed). The number of locations caps the category under sub-criterion (a). #> A continuing decline (sub-criterion b) was assumed rather than documented, as recommended for range-restricted taxa in converting landscapes; it should be confirmed against the trend of the specific habitat. As with the provisional category, this is a screening aid rather than a formal Red List assessment. #>  #> RECOMMENDATIONS FOR FORMAL ASSESSMENT #> Delimit the number of locations and assess severe fragmentation (subcondition a), defining 'location' by the most plausible threat (e.g. a fire season or climatic extreme per massif). #> Validate and refine the occurrences: confirm peripheral records, which drive the EOO, and expand sampling in undersampled terrain, which may bias the AOO downward. #> Obtain population size, structure and trend (supports subcriterion b(v) or Criteria C/D), currently absent from this screening. #> Submit the taxon to a formal assessment (CNCFlora / IUCN) and integrate this screening into protected-area management (fire and visitor management) where relevant. #>  #> CAVEATS AND LIMITATIONS #> The provisional category reflects range-size thresholds only and must not be reported as a final IUCN category. #> The AOO is sensitive to grid origin and to sampling effort; the EOO can be inflated by outlying or erroneous records. #>  #> REFERENCES #> - IUCN Standards and Petitions Committee (2024). Guidelines for Using the IUCN Red List Categories and Criteria, Version 16. Prepared by the Standards and Petitions Committee. https://www.iucnredlist.org/documents/RedListGuidelines.pdf #> - IUCN (2012). IUCN Red List Categories and Criteria: Version 3.1, Second edition. what: Sobreposição com Unidades de Conservação federais (offline)
title: NA
text: Esta versão (1.7.0) adiciona o cruzamento das métricas de distribuição com Unidades de Conservação (UC) federais ICMBio. Para cada espécie o pacote calcula fração de ocorrências dentro de UCs, o percentual EOO e AOO dentro de UCs, lista de UCs sobrepostas e — quando o MapBiomas é usado — o hábitat natural que também está dentro de UC (proteção efetiva), reportado sobre área total range e sobre parte dentro da UC. Há gráfico dedicado (plot_protection()), tabela (pa_table()) e uma aba aplicativo Shiny. Como WFS ICMBio é intermitente, os limites das UCs federais são lidos por padrão de uma cópia embutida (inst/extdata/ucs_federais.rds, resolução cheia), o que faz sobreposição funcionar offline. WFS continua disponível como alternativa automática, e é possível apontar um arquivo próprio de UCs com pa_src=. Fonte dos limites: ICMBio/INDE (licença PDDL, domínio público).

what: Nova metodologia de cálculo: EOO e AOO no padrão ConR
title: NA
text: Esta versão substitui o cálculo da Extensão de Ocorrência (EOO) e da Área de Ocupação (AOO) pelo método usado pacote ConR, alinhando o mappingAS com abordagem mais consolidada na literatura de avaliação de risco Critério B da IUCN.

previous_headings: Nova metodologia de cálculo: EOO e AOO no padrão ConR
title: NA
text: EOO (medição elipsoide / “spheroid”) O polígono convexo mínimo passa ser construído em coordenadas geográficas (longitude/latitude), com arestas densificadas via st_segmentize(20 km) para seguir grandes círculos, e área é medida diretamente sobre o elipsoide WGS84. Antes, medição era feita em uma projeção planar de áreas iguais (LAEA). AOO (mínimo sobre grades transladadas) contagem de células ocupadas passa ser calculada testando várias posições de grade transladadas aleatoriamente (n_rep = 30 por padrão), retornando menor contagem — o procedimento recomendado pelas diretrizes da IUCN e adotado pelo ConR. Antes, era usada uma única grade de origem fixa. Tratamento de casos degenerados (sem quebrar) - Menos de 3 pontos únicos: EOO retorna NA. - Pontos perfeitamente colineares: é adicionado um pequeno ruído (jitter) às coordenadas, como ConR, para que um polígono válido possa ser construído. - Qualquer outra falha na construção polígono retorna NA em vez de erro.
